title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 56-57). Grothendieck is building an axiomatic 'analysis situs', almost certainly an attempt at the 'topologie modérée' (tame topology) announced in Esquisse d'un programme (1984). The basic objects are 'ateliers' (workshops): structured collections of 'figures' in an underlying set L. Figures carry strata and 'multistrates', and there is an 'ombre' (shadow). The axioms are labelled H1-H3 and Atomicité 1-3.

Page 56 (Scholie). A set-theoretic ('ensembliste') atelier whose figures are of finite type is the same thing as a pair (L, M), where:
- L is a set;
- M is a set of 'elementary figures' in L, every sub-figure of an element of M being of finite type (automatic if the elements of M are finite figures);
- the axioms H1-H3 hold.
The atelier F is recovered as the sub-atelier of Fig(L) consisting of finite-type set-theoretic figures whose multistrata all lie in M.

Page 57.
1. Grothendieck observes that one should not expect F to be 'spécial' in the strong sense defined earlier, i.e. stable under arbitrary (co)limits, roughly arbitrary unions. His example: the family of all singletons {F_x = {{x}}}_{x in L} will in general not have its union/limit in F. Each point is a figure, but an arbitrary set of points is not.
2. The reasonable condition is therefore 'finiment spécial': stability only under finite such operations.
3. Using the axiom Atomicité 3, this condition reduces to a statement about order relations. Roughly, the relation ≼ (specialization/inclusion between figures) computed in L agrees with the set-theoretic relation ≼ restricted to M.
4. The margin note seems to record this condition ('condition que F ... relation ensembliste ... finiment spéciaux').

Corollary of the Scholie (started at the bottom). Set-theoretic, finitely special ateliers with finite-type figures correspond to pairs (L, M) with M a set of elementary figures satisfying:
- Atomicité 1 and 2: the singleton figures {{x}} lie in M, and multistrata of members of M lie in M again;
- every sub-figure of an x in M is of finite type.
F is then the set of figures generated (sentence cut off; there is no next-page transcription).

Purpose. The page separates a 'tame' finiteness condition (closure under finite operations only) from a 'wild' one (closure under arbitrary limits/unions), in order to classify tame set-theoretic models by generating data. This is conceptually the same move as passing from a topology to an o-minimal structure or a Boolean algebra of 'definable' sets. Points are definable, but arbitrary sets of points are not.
errors: No mathematical error detectable. The page is a working draft: the reduction 'finiment spécial ⇔ relation ≼_L equals set-theoretic ≼ on M (given Atomicité 3)' is asserted without proof. It depends on definitions (multistrate, ombre, Atomicité 3) on earlier pages not shown here.
The corollary breaks off mid-sentence ('Alors F est l'ensemble des ...'), so the final characterisation is incomplete on this page.

ideas.what: Ateliers of figures: an axiomatic framework for tame/stratified topology in which admissible 'figures' in a set L, with strata and multistrata, replace open sets
ideas.modern_name: closest: o-minimal structures / tame geometries; stratified spaces; 'topologie modérée'
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tame topology program: Grothendieck (Esquisse 1984); o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay-Steinhorn, Knight (1984-86); Shiota on tame/semialgebraic-type structures
ideas.where_published: Only the program, not the 'atelier' axiomatics, is in Esquisse d'un programme §5-6; the 1986 Analysis situs notes are unpublished

ideas.what: Rejection of closure under arbitrary limits/unions (strong 'spécial') in favour of 'finiment spécial'; the family of all singletons need not have its union admissible
ideas.modern_name: finite (not arbitrary) Boolean closure of definable sets; tameness excluding arbitrary unions of points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in o-minimality (definable sets form Boolean algebras, not complete ones)
ideas.where_published: Spirit of Esquisse §5 (critique of general topology); not in this form

ideas.what: Scholie/corollary: set-theoretic finitely special ateliers of finite type are classified by pairs (L, M) of a set and a set of elementary figures satisfying atomicity axioms
ideas.modern_name: presentation of a tame structure by generating 'basic' cells/figures (cf. cell decomposition generating definable sets)
ideas.usually_credited_to: No direct analogue known for this exact formulation

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatics of 'ateliers' (figures, multistrata, ombre, atomicity axioms, special vs finitely special) is an unpublished concrete attempt at his tame-topology program. Its relation to o-minimality and later tame-geometry axiomatics appears unexamined.
missed.quote: on ne s'attend pas en général que {F_x = {{x}}}_{x∈L} soit dans F ! La condition raisonnable dès lors, c'est que F soit finiment spéciaux.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historians and model theorists comparing Esquisse §5 with o-minimality usually treat the program as only sketched. These notes show a worked-out axiomatics with a classification of set-theoretic models by generators (L, M). That is useful for evaluating how close Grothendieck's own approach was to o-minimal structures or to newer frameworks such as tame geometry and condensed/stratified approaches.

deep.surprise_reason: The page belongs to an unpublished, little-studied axiomatisation of tame topology, which is of genuine historical interest. The specific content of this page, however, is a technical finiteness remark plus an incomplete classification corollary. It is not a striking standalone result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1-3 likely reads: 'ne s'attend pas que F soit un atelier spécial(?), au sens [complexe barré] fort où nous avons introduit ce terme, i.e. stable par lim. quelconques' (insertion above 'que' looks like 'finiment sp.').

'Vu la condition Atomicité 3' is correct; the following line is roughly 'cela signifie simplement que la relation ≼_L est la relation ≼_M ensembliste' (indices uncertain, possibly ≼ with subscript M under the symbol).
In the corollary: 'correspondent aux couples (L, M)' rather than 'correspondant à figures ... i.e. couple'; and 'satisfaisant Atomicité 1 et Atomicité 2' is underlined in the original.
'et tel que ∀x∈M, les sous-figures de L soient de t.f.' rather than 'ses figures de L sont de t.f.'
